facts.fact_text: On 17 May 2012 Mr Romanov took part in the 'Rainbow flash mob' event in St Petersburg.
The 'Rainbow flash mob' event in St Petersburg on 17 May 2012 had been authorised by the local authorities.
The 'Rainbow flash mob' event in St Petersburg on 17 May 2012 marked the International Day Against Homophobia and Transphobia.
A group of people protesting against the 'Rainbow flash mob' event gathered nearby during the event on 17 May 2012.
The local authorities had been notified in advance of the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg.
The local authorities deployed 165 police officers to maintain public order at the site of the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg.
The police did not intervene when counter-demonstrators started insulting the participants in the 'Rainbow flash mob' event on 17 May 2012.
About forty police officers were present at the site of the LGBTI demonstration in Voronezh on 20 January 2013 but did not intervene.
The police present at the scene of the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg did not intervene when counter-demonstrators attacked the participants.
Mr Starov, Ms Pitenova and Mr Fedorov decided to leave the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg.
While Mr Starov, Ms Pitenova and Mr Fedorov were walking away from the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg, about thirty counter-demonstrators ran up to them and started beating them.
The police called an ambulance three hours after taking the applicants to the police station following the attacks on 29 June 2013.
Mr Fedorov and Ms Levina complained that they had been apprehended and detained unlawfully, before the start of the authorised demonstration of 12 October 2013 in St Petersburg.
On 26 February 2015 the Kuybyshevskiy District Court of St Petersburg dismissed the complaint by Mr Fedorov and Ms Levina that they had been apprehended and detained unlawfully on 12 October 2013.
On 29 April 2016 the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation finally upheld the Kuybyshevskiy District Court of St Petersburg's decision dismissing the complaint by Mr Fedorov and Ms Levina.

The local authorities had been notified in advance of the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg.

At 1.55 p.m. on 12 October 2013, five minutes before the demonstration started, the police began apprehending the participants, including Mr Fedorov, Mr Prokopenko and Ms Levina, on the grounds that they had used foul language.
At 2.30 p.m. on 12 October 2013 the police escorted Mr Fedorov, Mr Prokopenko and Ms Levina to a police station.
The police were deployed to maintain public order during the 'Rainbow flash mob' event on 17 May 2012.
About forty police officers were present at the site of the LGBTI demonstration in Voronezh on 20 January 2013 but did not intervene.
The police present at the scene of the demonstration of 29 June 2013 in St Petersburg did not intervene when counter-demonstrators attacked the participants.
The parties submitted no further information about any preliminary measures which had been put in place to protect the demonstrators at the 'Rainbow flash mob' event on 17 May 2012.

Between July 2013 and December 2015 the police repeatedly refused to open a criminal investigation into battery committed for hate motives under Article 116 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation in relation to the attacks of 29 June 2013, citing a 'hostile attitude of people of heterosexual orientation towards members of the LGBTI community'.

The prosecutor quashed the police's repeated decisions not to open a criminal investigation into the attacks of 29 June 2013 each time and ordered additional inquiries, emphasising the need to identify and question eyewitnesses of the attacks on the applicants.

Following the last decision by the police on 23 December 2015 not to initiate a criminal investigation into the attacks of 29 June 2013, the police did not carry out the measures ordered by the prosecutor.

On 24 December 2013 the investigator refused an application by Mr Chechetkin's lawyer for the perpetrators' actions to be classified under Article 111 § 3 (a) and (b) of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation as actions committed by a group of persons for motives of hatred or enmity towards LGBTI people.
On 6 March 2015 the Leninskiy District Court of St Petersburg dismissed an appeal by Mr Chechetkin against the investigator's decision of 16 July 2014 to suspend the investigation.
On 6 March 2015 the Leninskiy District Court of St Petersburg dismissed a further application by Mr Chechetkin to have the perpetrators' actions classified as motivated by hatred.
The investigators suspended and resumed the investigation into the attack on Mr Chechetkin multiple times, most recently on 7 October 2017, without achieving any tangible results.
